items.title: Live: Commonwealth seeking $2 billion in damages from 3M over firefighting foam chemicals
items.description: The Commonwealth sues the manufacturer of the firefighting foam containing PFAS chemicals which has contaminated 28 Defence bases across Australia. Follow live.

items.title: Batteries are the key to unlocking an energy revolution, and one state is racing ahead
items.description: Western Australia in particular is proving to the world that grid-scale batteries are no longer a complementary technology but can play a central role in power grids.

items.title: Housing investors are increasingly older and wealthier, Reserve Bank research shows
items.description: Reserve Bank research shows property investment has become skewed towards higher-income households and is dominated by baby boomers.

items.title: 'We need to talk about sex': Young people call for sex ed to grow up
items.description: A long-running survey of Australian teens has identified falling condom use and unwanted sex as major concerns for young people starting relationships.

items.title: Woman who returned from Syria charged with terrorism offences
items.description: The Australian Federal Police will provide a briefing to the media shortly.

items.title: Live: 'Does Trump have an end goal anymore?' ABC experts answer your questions on Iran war
items.description: ABC experts are answering questions abut the Iran war as the conflict enters its fourth month with no clear end in sight. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: US Justice Department launches criminal probe into E Jean Carroll
items.description: The probe is focused on whether Carroll committed perjury in testimony tied to two civil lawsuits that she won against Mr Trump — one tied to ‌her allegations that he sexually abused her in a New York department store.

items.title: Israel kills new Hamas militant chief, along with his wife and children
items.description: An Israeli air strike in Gaza has killed new Hamas leader Mohammed Odeh, his wife and two of his children, the militant group has confirmed.

items.title: Man joins brother and late mother's reconciliation journey after discovering he is Indigenous
items.description: Iain Seymour didn't realise he was Aboriginal until he discovered he was adopted and learned that his mother played a key role in a memorial to the long-term effects of the Stolen Generations. Warning: This story contains images of Indigenous people who have died.

items.title: Live: ASX opens lower as price of oil drops
items.description: The Australian share market opens lower as the price of oil drops. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal sacked by ABC
items.description: Mahmood Fazal has been sacked by the ABC following an internal investigation into an appearance on a podcast hosted by a former underworld figure, managing director Hugh Marks says.

items.title: 'Remarkable' large funnel cloud spotted in regional Victoria
items.description: The Bureau of Meteorology says it is unusual to see large funnel clouds so far west in Victoria.

items.title: Mother whose two children died suddenly calls for genetic testing
items.description: A Perth woman who lost two children to an extremely rare medical condition calls for mandatory genetic testing for children whose cause of death is uncertain.

items.title: Young saviour and an answered prayer deliver Blues incredible Origin win
items.description: When the Blues needed heroes to get on top of the Maroons in State of Origin I, they turned to a debutante and the oldest player on the field.

items.title: How women composers defied expectations and transformed the music world
items.description: From Hildegard von Bingen to Hildur Guðnadóttir, here are some of the most influential women of the music world in history and today.

items.title: Why this photo has been terrifying the internet for years
items.description: Forget about slashers and body horror — the next evolution of fright stems from an fluorescent-lit room.

items.title: Quiz: Can you identify Aussie TV shows from a single frame?
items.description: How well do you know your Neighbours from your Deadloch? Take our single-frame Australian TV quiz to find out.

items.title: Stars involved in handshake drama as Rybakina exits Roland-Garros
items.description: There is no love lost between Tamara Korpatsch and Wang Xinyu after a testy match as Elena Rybakina's hopes of another grand slam title go up in smoke.

items.title: Accused exit trafficker fraudulently cancelled wife's visa application, police say
items.description: The man, who left his wife in India and did not return for the birth of his son, is the first person in the ACT to be charged with the crime.

items.title: 15yo Indian phenom smashes Cummins to set new IPL sixes record
items.description: Australia's captain feels the brunt of the pain as Indian sensational Vaibhav Sooryavanshi continues his phenomenal IPL form.

items.title: Council to demolish in-demand childcare centre for open space
items.description: A childcare centre's director says relocation had been promised for years until late last year, when the council decided there was no feasible site in the area.

items.title: Hugh Marks denies 'threat' to force ABC news director out of role
items.description: ABC managing director Hugh Marks says he did not "make threats" to terminate departing news boss Justin Stevens, as senators question his sudden departure.

items.title: Video shows divers finding five Laos cavers alive, two remain missing
items.description: A rescue mission has been underway for more than a week to find seven people who entered a cave in central Laos before becoming trapped in a landslide triggered by heavy rain.

items.title: UK's social media ban could be harsher than Australia's. Here's how it compares
items.description: The UK could become the latest nation to implement a social media ban, after British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer vowed to introduce a "game changer" policy.

items.title: Matthew Perry's assistant jailed for role in Friends actor's death
items.description: Matthew Perry's live-in personal assistant, who had a central role in the Friends star's descent into ketamine addiction and injected him with the fatal dose of the drug, has been sentenced to three years and five months in prison.
